2. The plaintiff brought the suit for a declaration that the order dated 25.3.69 passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner; Revenue setting aside the certificate sale held on 16-4-60 in Certificate Case No. 398 of 1959-60 was void, without jurisdiction and not binding on the plaintiff. 

 3. The plaintiff's case was that the suit land belonged to Pulin Behari Maitra and the rent for the year 1962 amounting to Taka 19.69 paisa was in arrear. Upon the State Acquisition, the then Government of East Pakistan started Certificate Case No. 398 of 1959-60 against Pulin Behari Maitra for the said arrear rent and the suit land was sold in Execution of the Certificate and auction purchased by the plaintiff on 16-6-60. The sale was confirmed on 16-6-60 and the plaintiff got delivery of possession of the suit land on 7-11-60 and has been in continuous possession of the same. The defendant No. 1, the then Administrative Officer of the Evacuee Property Management Committee brought Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 1960-61 under section 23 of the P.D.R. Act for setting aside the sale which was dismissed by the Certificate officer. The defendant No. 1 preferred appeal No. 32 of 1961-62 before the Joint Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur which was dismissed on 8-11-62. The defendant No. 1 then preferred revision case No. 275 of 1962 before the Commissioner who allowed the revision case, set aside the judgment of the Joint Deputy Commissioner and remanded the case to the Certificate officer for fresh adjudication. The certificate officer after hearing the case afresh dismissed the Mies. Case on 23-12-63 and defendant No. 1 preferred appeal No. 14/65-66 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Rangpur on 3-3-66. The appeal having been filed after a delay of 70 days the Additional Deputy Commissioner dismissed the appeal as being barred by limitation. The defendant Nos. 1 then submitted a revisional application before the same Additional Deputy Commissioner on 28-5-66 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner allowed the revisional application and set aside the certificate sale by his order dated 25-3-69 which was illegal and without jurisdiction because after once disposing of the appeal the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) had no jurisdiction to allow the revision. Hence the suit. 

 6. Mr. Mokhter Hossain, the learned advocate appearing for the appellant, submitted that when the same Additional Deputy Commissioner had disposed of and dismissed the appeal filed by the defendant No. 1 against the certificate sale that tent amounted to his confirmation of the order of the certificate officer in confirming the sale and so the appellate order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner stood merged with the original judgment of the certificate officer and as such the same Additional Deputy Commissioner could not revise the said order of the Certificate officer which tent amounted to revision of his own order as he had dismissed the appeal. On this point Mr. Sultan Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondents, submitted that the Additional Deputy Commissioner did not actually adjudicate on the appeal but simply dismissed the appeal as being barred by limitation without going into the merits of the case and as such in this situation it could not be said that the order of dismissal of the appeal passed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner merged into the order of the Certificate officer. As a matter of fact the appeal that was filed by the defendant No. 1 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner was not entertained by him because it was a time barred appeal having been filed 70 days beyond the period of limitation. So the appeal was dismissed as being barred by limitation without considering the facts and merits of the appeal. In such a situation it cannot be said that the order of dismissal of the appeal on the ground of limitation amounted to dismissal of the appeal on merits and as such the order of dismissal of the appeal as being barred by limitation can not mean that the Additional Deputy Commissioner decided the appeal on merits and that his order amounted to confirmation of the sale or confirmation of the order of the Certificate Officer dismissing the sale setting aside case. So the contention of Mr. Mokhtar Hossain on this point does not stand. In this position, the Additional Deputy Commissioner did not commit any illegality in exercising his power under section 53 of the P.D.R. Act and revising the order of the Certificate officer and in setting aside the sale. Had he had heard the appeal and decided the appeal on merit then only he would be precluded from exercising revisional jurisdiction as that would amount to a revision of his own order. But here the case was different because the Additional Deputy Commissioner did not entertain the appeal but dismissed it outright as the appeal was filed 70 days beyond the period of limitation. So the Additional Deputy Commissioner had no scope to consider or decide on the merit of the appeal or on the Merit of the certificate sale and the order Of the Certificate officer refusing to set aside the sale. 

 7. Of course it may he said that the defendant No. 1 could not-seek any redress by way of revision under section 53 of the P.D.R. Act without availing the remedy of preferring appeal under section 51 of the P.D.R. Act within the prescribed time and that the defendant No. 1 having failed to prefer the appeal within the prescribed time he had no right to seek revision under section 53 of the P.D.R. Act because it is an established principle of law that the remedy of appeal has to be followed in the first instance where such remedy is available and where it is not open to a party to prefer an appeal then only the remedy by way of revision can be resorted to. In this case, as I have already found the defendant No. 1 did not prefer the appeal within the prescribed time and thus failed to avail of the remedy of appeal that was available to him. In such a situation it can be rightly said that the defendant No. 1 had no legal right to seek revision under section 53 of the P.D.R. Act. But even then on a perusal of the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, it is found that the Additional Deputy Commissioner in revising the order of the Certificate officer and in setting aside the sale exercised his Suo motu power under section 53 of the P.D.R. Act. He has repeatedly and categorically mentioned in the order that he was making the revision suo motu. Section 53 of the P.D.R. Act authorises the Collector and the Additional Collector to revise the order passed by a Certificate officer even without any application on that behalf. Thus it is found that-the Additional Deputy Commissioner acted within jurisdiction in passing the order of revision and in setting aside the sale and there was no illegality in the order.
